_comment: Single source of truth for the MTCO AI Roadmap. Ken appends proposals here; app.py injects it into dashboard.html at render. Stages: Proposed, Scoped, Planned, Building, Testing, Shipped.

projects.name: Auto Updating Schedule for AES
projects.summary: Auto-updates the AES schedule and diary from Big Change job entries so the management software and the besp...
projects.scope: Auto-updates the AES schedule and diary from Big Change job entries so the management software and the bespoke planner match at all times, eliminating the need for manual data entry and removing the risk of mis-communication and human error.
projects.how: Reads job entries from Big Change and automatically syncs or pushes them into the AES management software and bespoke planner/diary, so both systems match continuously without manual re-entry.

who.how: saves significant time currently spent on manual diary entries

who.who: reduces human error and mis-communication between systems

projects.name: AES Service Agent
projects.summary: Answer service scheduling questions from Big Change ("when is the service at WA4 for this customer") in nat...
projects.scope: Answer service scheduling questions from Big Change ("when is the service at WA4 for this customer") in natural language. If the service has already happened, it pulls the completed job sheet and presents it to the person asking. Saves the service team and customers from manually searching Big Change for service records.
projects.how: Interrogates Big Change data to find scheduled service jobs by customer or location (e.g. postcode WA4), returning the next due service date and type. For completed services, it pulls the job sheet from Big Change and presents it. Could be a chat interface that answers natural language service queries.

who.how: quicker answers to service schedule queries
no more manual digging through Big Change for service dates
faster responses when they ask "when's my next service"

projects.name: Ainscough Haulage Driver Tracking Agent
projects.summary: Answer delivery tracking questions ("where is the driver for today's WA4 delivery") in natural language and...
projects.scope: Answer delivery tracking questions ("where is the driver for today's WA4 delivery") in natural language and provide a shareable live-tracking link so customers can see delivery progress in real time without calling the office. For deliveries due today, reports how far away the driver is.
projects.how: Queries Big Change for delivery jobs by customer and date, reads driver tracking data (if Big Change supports GPS tracking or integrates with a telematics platform). For in-progress deliveries it reports the driver's distance from site. If Big Change provides a tracking URL, the agent surfaces the shareable link that can be sent externally to customers. Could also send automated SMS/email tracking links at dispatch.

who.how: self-serve tracking of deliveries without ringing the office
far fewer "where's my driver" calls
professional, transparent delivery experience

projects.name: The Pizza Tracker - Automated Customer Delivery Cycle
projects.summary: A fully automated customer communication cycle covering every stage from ordering through to delivery and c...
projects.scope: A fully automated customer communication cycle covering every stage from ordering through to delivery and collection - 'like tracking a Domino's pizza'. Covers: intelligent automated ordering (building on the site planner), order confirmation, customer PO checked against order and contract to flag issues before production starts, auto-notification 48 hours before delivery (last chance to modify without charge), quality-checked cabin photos shared with the customer, 'on its way' notification with live tracking link, and delivery confirmation with driver pictures and POD. Extends to collections, repairs and servicing.
projects.how: The system connects Kensite's order/contract data (MCS), the production/prep schedule and the transport planner (Big Change/AES) into a customer-facing notification pipeline. At each stage - order placed, PO validated against order, production started, 48-hour lock-in approaching, unit dispatched with tracking, delivery complete with POD - an automated message or portal update is triggered. Customers receive a link (like a Domino's Pizza Tracker) to see where their cabin is in the process without phoning the hire desk. The same cycle applies to collections, repairs and servicing.

who.how: full visibility without phoning in, pre-emptive updates at every stage - a genuinely pre-emptive experience. Hire desk and Ops team: fewer inbound calls chasing order status, admin issues caught and resolved before production starts. Transport team: automated POD distribution replaces manual chasing.

projects.name: Kensite Technicals - Technical Help Triage & Knowledge Hub
projects.summary: Provides an email and WhatsApp channel for technical help where initial repair requests are triaged with ac...
projects.scope: Provides an email and WhatsApp channel for technical help where initial repair requests are triaged with access to all equipment manuals to avoid unnecessary call outs. If a call out is unavoidable, a repair is logged. Also helps our own teams by importing all job sheets with the fixes made, building a knowledge sharing database that builds on the common fixes datasheet that Mitch started.
projects.how: A triage system reads incoming technical help requests via email and WhatsApp, cross-references equipment manuals and imported job sheet history to suggest common fixes, and only escalates to a call out when no match is found. Every completed job sheet is imported to grow a searchable knowledge base of fixes, building on the common fixes datasheet Mitch started.

who.how: fewer unnecessary call outs and access to shared fix knowledge
faster technical issue resolution
logged repairs and trend data from job sheet imports

projects.name: Ken, AI operations agent
projects.summary: Answers staff by email, checks MCS and Big Change, sends paperwork and creates quotes.
projects.scope: Ken is Kensite's AI colleague on email. Staff ask him in plain English and he looks things up in MCS (contracts, what is on hire, rates, quotes, purchase orders, invoices), fetches proof of delivery photographs from Big Change, attaches hire contracts, quote and invoice copies, drafts and creates quotes in MCS, searches and reads the document library, keeps the IMS register moving and logs what he cannot yet do on his own wishlist.
projects.how: A Pydantic AI agent polling his own mailbox every ten seconds. Each email is triaged, then answered by a model equipped with a fixed toolbox of Python functions that talk to MCS RM-web, Big Change, Graph and the SharePoint library. Anything that writes or sends pauses for the requester's approval unless they explicitly asked. Trusted staff get the full toolbox; named outside guests get a separate agent holding only the tools they are granted. He deploys his own new versions and keeps a status file and audit trail.

who.how: Contract, hire and paperwork questions answered in minutes without opening MCS
Proof of delivery photographs and movement checks on request
Invoice copies, purchase order lookups and Big Change invoice consolidation
One place to see what the AI estate is doing, and a wishlist of what it should do next

projects.name: Daily delivery and collection notices
projects.summary: Each evening the next day's movements go to the yard and haulage, checked against the prep schedule.
projects.scope: Every evening at 16:30 the following day's deliveries and collections are pulled from MCS, the assets on each are listed and grouped by contract, checked against the prep schedule, and emailed to the yard and transport team so the day is planned before anyone arrives.
projects.how: A scheduled Python worker on Ken's machine runs the MCS delivery search and collections report, applies the yard's own rules (fleet sales and service only contracts skipped, fleet numbers shown where allocated), compares against the prep schedule on GitHub and sends from Ken's mailbox through Graph.

who.how: The next day's loading list ready first thing, without anyone compiling it
Collections and deliveries in one list, matched to the prep schedule
Discrepancies between MCS and the prep schedule surfaced the evening before

projects.name: Prep Schedule app
projects.summary: A live web app for the yard's prep schedule, with request queues that workers pick up.
projects.scope: The yard's prep schedule as a Streamlit web app instead of a spreadsheet: on hires, off hires and site moves by day, units, haulage and notes, editable from any device. It also carries request queues for quotes, copy invoices, live hire reports and materials, which automations pick up within minutes.
projects.how: Streamlit Community Cloud app deployed from GitHub with its data in JSON files in the same repo, written through the GitHub contents API. Automations on Ken's machine poll the queue files and act on them; the MCS discrepancy check reconciles the schedule against MCS every ten minutes.

who.how: One schedule everyone sees, kept in step with MCS
Requests for quotes, invoices and reports raised in the app and fulfilled automatically
A single view of the week's movements

projects.name: Prep schedule and MCS discrepancy check
projects.summary: Every ten minutes the prep schedule is reconciled against MCS and gaps are flagged or fixed.
projects.scope: Compares what is booked in MCS (deliveries, collections and split deliveries) with what is on the prep schedule, auto adds movements the schedule is missing and emails a discrepancy list for anything that does not match.
projects.how: A scheduled worker runs the MCS delivery search and collections report, URL decodes split contract references, matches each MCS movement to at most one prep entry, writes safe additions back to the schedule's JSON on GitHub and emails the rest from Ken's mailbox.

who.how: No movement arrives that the schedule did not know about
Booking errors caught within ten minutes rather than on the day

projects.name: Live hire report on request
projects.summary: Ask for a customer's live hire report in the app and the PDF and Excel arrive by email.
projects.scope: Anyone can request a customer live hire report from the prep schedule app. The worker matches the customer to their MCS account, runs the report in both formats and emails the branded PDF and a clean Excel to the requester.
projects.how: Polls the request queue every seven minutes, fuzzy matches the customer name to MCS accounts, runs user report 59 for the PDF and report 61 for the data, rebuilds the Excel in the agreed column format and sends from Ken's mailbox.

who.how: Live hire reports for customers in minutes without touching MCS
Consistent branded reports to send on

projects.name: Copy invoices on request
projects.summary: Request copy invoices in the app and one email arrives with every PDF attached.
projects.scope: The hire desk queues copy invoice requests in the prep schedule app; the worker pulls each invoice PDF from MCS and sends one email per request with every invoice attached.
projects.how: Polls the queue every five minutes, fetches each invoice through the MCS report endpoint using the Shared Toolbox's document unwrapper, and emails from Ken's mailbox through Graph.

who.how: Copy invoices out to customers the same hour they are asked for
No more digging invoices out of MCS one by one

projects.name: Materials purchase orders
projects.summary: Materials requests are matched to supplier catalogues and invoice history and raised as purchase orders for review.
projects.scope: Materials requested from the prep schedule app are matched to the Danfast catalogue and to what Kensite has actually bought before, priced, and routed into a purchase order in Zahara with the evidence shown beside each line so the approver can overrule it.
projects.how: A scheduled worker reads the materials queue, scores each line against the supplier portal crawl and the invoice history (invoice evidence wins where it is clearly better), builds the order through the Zahara API and emails the approver from Ken's mailbox.

who.how: Orders drafted in minutes with the reasoning visible
Materials requested from the same app as everything else
Cleaner purchase order data and fewer mismatched invoices

projects.name: Quote trends workbook
projects.summary: A branded Excel of the last three months of quotes: what, who, how much and conversion.
projects.scope: Pulls every quote raised in the last three months from MCS and writes a Kensite branded workbook: headline numbers, monthly trend and conversion, unit types quoted, top customers and quotes by salesperson, with the raw quotes behind it.
projects.how: Runs the MCS Quote Analysis report plus each quote's detail page over HTTP, then builds charted sheets with openpyxl. Read only; nothing is written back.

who.how: See what is being quoted and to whom without a manual export
Conversion and pipeline trend on demand

projects.name: Weekly check up pack
projects.summary: The Monday meeting's figures built automatically every week from MCS.
projects.scope: Builds the weekly check up for the Monday meeting: run rate, units on hire, yield, the week's on and off hire movement and projections, from seven MCS reports, and sends it as a pack.
projects.how: A scheduled builder pulls seven MCS user reports through the Shared Toolbox, applies Nathan's definitions of hire figure and yield, renders the pack and emails it from Ken's mailbox at 14:00 each week, with an offline test suite behind it.

who.how: The Monday numbers ready without a morning of spreadsheet work
Consistent definitions week to week

projects.name: IMS register review reminders
projects.summary: Owners are reminded of the documents, certificates and assessments they have due for review.
projects.scope: Reads the Master IMS Register, finds every document, certificate, assessment or process overdue for review or expiring soon, and emails each owner a reminder listing only their items, every morning.
projects.how: A scheduled read only worker opens the register workbook from the synced library, groups items by owner and sends from Ken's mailbox through Graph at 09:35 daily. Ken can also read the register and plan closures when asked.

who.how: A short personal list rather than a 400 row register
Reviews kept current ahead of ISO audits

projects.name: RAMS and lift plan generation
projects.summary: A customer's risk assessment or a job's details become a fully branded Kensite RAMS pack in minutes.
projects.scope: Turns an uploaded risk assessment, or a customer, site and job brief, into a complete Kensite RAMS or generic lift plan pack in house style: risk assessment, method statement and lift diagram appendices.
projects.how: Claude skills encoding the Kensite templates, wording and brand rules produce the Word documents from the source material, with the author checking before issue.

who.how: Consistent, complete RAMS packs without starting from a blank template
Delivery RAMS for a new customer turned round the same day
Lift plans issued before the crane arrives

projects.name: Site Builder compound drawings
projects.summary: Customers lay out their own compound online and get a branded Kensite drawing back automatically.
projects.scope: A public web app where a customer drags Kensite units onto a site plan. Each saved layout becomes a branded Kensite PDF drawing automatically, Ken issues the drawing reference and emails it, and a bill of quantities can be read straight off the drawing for quoting.
projects.how: Streamlit app on GitHub; a watcher on Ken's machine turns new or re saved drawings into PDFs, files every issued version by reference and reports circulation. Ken picks up requests every three minutes, issues references and keeps the app awake overnight.

who.how: A drawing and quantities from the customer's own hand, ready to quote
See their compound before they order
Drawings that match what actually goes on the lorry

projects.name: Weekly clocking report
projects.summary: The week's clockings from InfoTime become a branded timesheet workbook every Monday.
projects.scope: Logs into the InfoTime clock system each Monday, collects the previous Saturday to Friday period for every current employee and saves a Kensite branded Excel workbook to the shared Yard Timesheets folder.
projects.how: A scheduled scraper walks the timesheet pages (the system's own export is broken), builds the workbook with openpyxl and files it, with a failure email if anything stops it.

who.how: Timesheets ready first thing Monday, every week
One consistent workbook to check against

projects.name: MCS contact clean up
projects.summary: Finds missing emails and phone numbers for MCS contacts from the enquiries mailbox, for approval.
projects.scope: Audits MCS customer contacts for missing email addresses and phone numbers, then searches the enquiries mailbox for them and writes a proposals spreadsheet a person approves before anything is entered.
projects.how: Two read only scripts: an audit of MCS contacts, and an Outlook scan that matches names to addresses and numbers. Nothing is written to MCS or the mailbox.

who.how: Contact records that can actually be used to send quotes and invoices
Fewer bounced emails and unreachable customers

projects.name: Big Change haulage cost reconciliation
projects.summary: Ainscough Haulage invoices on Big Change matched to the MCS contracts and orders they belong to.
projects.scope: Reconciles haulage job costs invoiced through Big Change against MCS: each invoice is matched to its purchase order and contract, priced against MCS's own order, categorised, and the unmatched remainder reported with the reason, so haulage cost sits on the right job.
projects.how: A worker Ken loads on request runs the Big Change financial documents report and MCS reports 60 and 63, matches on the exact purchase order number with typing variations forgiven and never on similarity, and produces the reconciliation workbook with notes on every row.

who.how: Haulage cost allocated to the right contracts, with the exceptions explained
Visibility of what Ainscough Haulage has billed against each job

projects.name: Transport capacity alerts
projects.summary: The enquiries desk is told the moment a day in the AES transport planner fills up or frees up.
projects.scope: Watches the AES Transport Planner for days marked at capacity and emails the enquiries desk only when something changes: a day newly full, or a full day that now has space.
projects.how: Runs every twenty minutes, reads the planner's Google Sheet through a service account, fingerprints the state so unchanged runs send nothing, and emails from Ken's mailbox.

who.how: Never promise a date the planner cannot take
Freed capacity resold the same day

projects.name: Big Change invoice search and consolidation
projects.summary: Ask Ken for AES invoices from Big Change and get them collated or consolidated into totals, with a spreadsheet.
projects.scope: AES staff email Ken to find, list, total or consolidate Big Change invoices by customer, order number, job type, month or site, and get a statement and a two sheet workbook back. Read only: nothing is raised or changed in Big Change.
projects.how: Ken's guest agent for named AES contacts holds only the Big Change invoice tools, which query the Big Change web services API and build the workbook. Guests never reach anything of Kensite's.

who.how: Consolidated invoice statements in minutes
One clear statement instead of a pile of invoices

projects.name: MTCO AI Roadmap tracker
projects.summary: This dashboard: every AI project across the group, by company and stage, kept current by Ken.
projects.scope: A group wide view of AI implementation, impact and planned rollout across MTCO's companies. Named staff email Ken an idea and he files it as Proposed under the right company and business function, asking for what it does, how it works and who it benefits when the email does not say; he can also move, edit and remove entries as projects progress.
projects.how: A Streamlit app deployed from GitHub that renders a self contained dashboard fed by data/roadmap.json in the same repo. Ken writes to that file through the GitHub contents API with the change history kept in git; a publish script in the Automations folder rolls out changes to the app itself.

who.how: One honest picture of AI across the companies
A place to put ideas and see them progress
No hand maintenance of the tracker

projects.name: ESG & Compliance Dashboard for Site Setups
projects.summary: Generates a unified ESG and compliance report for each site compound, pulling together power insights from...
projects.scope: Generates a unified ESG and compliance report for each site compound, pulling together power insights from all providers into one clean Kensite Site Compound Report, plus a compliance dashboard covering legionella testing, water usage, electrical testing and other site compliance data.
projects.how: Ingests power usage and insight data from whatever power provider a site uses (renewable or traditional), normalises it alongside Kensite's own compliance test results (legionella testing, water usage, electrical testing, PAT testing), and presents everything as a branded dashboard or report per site compound setup.

who.how: one clean ESG report instead of multiple from different providers. Kensite sales and hire desk: strengthens the value proposition and supports the goal of managing power supply for customers. HSEQ team: consolidated compliance tracking across all live sites.

projects.name: Off-Hire Inbox Monitor & Daily Summary
projects.summary: Monitors the enquiries inbox for emails about the off-hire and collection of kit, then produces a daily sum...
projects.scope: Monitors the enquiries inbox for emails about the off-hire and collection of kit, then produces a daily summary email to the team showing time received, customer, site, assumed contract number, whether it has been actioned, and whether it has been replied to (and by who). Helps the team track and better manage off-hires.
projects.how: Ken reads the enquiries inbox throughout the day, identifies emails related to off-hire and collection requests, extracts key details (timestamp, customer, site, contract reference), checks the current status in MCS and the prep schedule, and compiles a single end-of-day summary email for the whole team.

who.how: full visibility of off-hire requests coming in, whether anyone has picked them up, and what still needs actioning. Hire desk: one daily picture of outgoing collections rather than scattered inbox threads.
